recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit. Restoring the original List narrative wording would conflict with later Composition.section.text decisions; future changes should be treated as new document-presentation policy work, not additional FHIR-5154 application.
issue_request: FHIR-5154 was Published with resolution Persuasive with Modification. The ballot comment asked the Structured Documents work group to identify or add specification language addressing the wholeness of FHIR documents and the status of narrative content when a Composition and its section-supporting resources are wrapped into a Document.
initial_application: The issue was applied in git-svn commit 11e32d8670a345d8c934c76c3d204222b3716303, which added wording to the then-current Composition introduction saying that when a Composition and its Lists are wrapped into a Document, the List narrative is part of the attested content and an indivisible part of the document.
additional_context: Later final decisions changed the representation without losing the rule. FHIR-12963 added general clinical-document principles, including wholeness; FHIR-15723 clarified attested-content wording on the Documents guide; FHIR-7404 moved section narrative into Composition.section.text and removed stale List/section.content language on the combined branch; and FHIR-17109 clarified that wholeness does not require inlining every referenced resource.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Active current source states that a document is a whole unit, defines the document presentation as subject, Composition, and Composition.section.text narratives, points attesters to that presentation, and says List.text is not part of the attested document presentation unless incorporated into Composition narrative or section.text.

related_jiras.note: Superseded the old Composition.section.content/List narrative model with Composition.section.text and fixed stale source notes on the combined branch.
Clarified Documents guide attested-content wording and the distinction between document presentation and other included resources.
Added clinical document principles, including wholeness, to document-related guidance.
Resolved no-change and clarified that wholeness does not require inlining every referenced resource.
